note: SYMPTOM: the recursive TraceRay is handed the closest-hit shader's OWN inout payload object instead of a copy of it. Clause 1 binds the payload parameter name from the entry function's `define` line with a backreference and requires that exact SSA value to be the payload operand of `dx.op.traceRay` -- i.e. the callee's payload aliases the caller's, so the HLSL copy-in/copy-out that `inout` requires has been elided. Clause 2 anchors that the source's `payload.data0 += 1` survived to DXIL, so a module missing the increment entirely cannot score as the reported symptom. Its register class is `%[\w.]+` rather than `%\d+` because v1.4.1907 emits named SSA values (`%.i09 = add i32 %.i08, 1`); a numeric-only anchor scored that release no-match for a reason unrelated to the symptom. Both clauses are POSITIVE, so a compile that failed to parse emits no DXIL and cannot satisfy them -- this predicate has no absence clause and therefore no vacuous-truth direction (SKILL step 4). It is also insensitive to SSA numbering and to instruction scheduling, which is what makes it comparable across twenty releases. WHY THIS IS THE SYMPTOM: HLSL parameters are copy-in/copy-out, so `TraceRay(..., payload)` must trace with a distinct payload object; DXR gives caller and callee separate payload storage. The measured control pair is the reporter's own pair of shaders, run on the same release with the same flags: control-workaround.hlsl (their working variant, which copies into a local `new_payload` first) scores NO-MATCH on v1.6.2104 and v1.6.2106 while repro.hlsl MATCHES there, so the predicate reproduces the exact distinction the issue reports rather than firing on every raytracing shader. CONTROLS: control-workaround.hlsl --expect no-match (known-good code, must not fire; it fires on nothing at any release); control-increment-after-trace.hlsl --expect no-match on ground truth (a shader that legitimately traces with an un-incremented payload -- on a fixed compiler it still uses a distinct temporary, so it proves the predicate is keyed on payload ALIASING and not merely on 'the traced payload lacks the increment'). NOTE: on the affected releases that control MATCHES too, and correctly so -- it also hands `TraceRay` its own incoming payload, so it is subject to the same defect; see manual-case-release-matrix.txt. The control that discriminates on the affected releases is control-workaround.hlsl, which scores no-match on all 20 stable releases and on ground truth. Also control-hello.hlsl --expect no-match, which doubles as the feature-presence probe proving every probed release can compile lib_6_3 DXR at all.
